claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and the children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I have one child - Alex, who is 7 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 7 years old.

Now, to continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

Since you're living abroad, I need to ask:

**Are you a Crown servant (such as someone working for the UK government abroad, in the civil service, armed forces, or similar roles)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant. I'm not working for the UK government or in the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since you're living abroad and not a Crown servant, I need to ask one more question to fully assess your situation:

**Which country are you currently living in?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

According to UK Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. Additionally, if you live abroad, you may be able to get Child Benefit only if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant.

Since you:
- Live in Spain (not in the UK)
- Are not a Crown servant
- Have one child, Alex (age 7)

Unfortunately, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit under the current rules. The rules specify that Child Benefit is available to those living abroad only in specific circumstances, such as being a Crown servant or living in certain designated countries. Spain is not listed as one of the countries where you can claim Child Benefit if you're not a Crown servant.

To get definitive information about whether Spain qualifies or to explore any other options that might apply to your specific circumstances, I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly, as there may be specific provisions I'm not aware of.
